title: Card game deck, Fisher Yates shuffle and rules engine
when: A card game needs a correct deck model, an unbiased shuffle, dealing, and a rules engine for moves like drawing, playing and scoring hands.
prompt:
Goal: An unbiased, testable deck plus rules written as small check functions, not scattered ifs.
Steps:
1. cards.mjs: SUITS = ["clubs", "diamonds", "hearts", "spades"], ranks 1 to 13, card ids like "H12" so state stays JSON.
2. shuffle(a, rng): for (let i = a.length - 1; i > 0; i--) { const j = Math.floor(rng() * (i + 1)); swap a[i] and a[j] }, with rng injected for tests.
3. Never shuffle with array.sort(() => Math.random() - 0.5); it is biased and engine dependent.
4. Piles are named arrays in state: deck, discard, hands per player, tableau columns; deal(state, n) takes from the top, the end of the array.
5. Rules are functions canPlay(state, card, target) returning true or a reason string, and play(state, move) returning a new state.
6. Scoring helpers per game, for example handValue counting aces as 11 and lowering them to 1 while the total is above 21.
7. Each card shows rank, suit symbol and text (aria-label "Queen of hearts"); suits differ by shape as well as red and black.
Quality bar:
- Over 60000 shuffles of 3 cards each of the 6 orders appears about 10000 times, within 5 percent.
- The card count stays 52 after any sequence of moves.
Pitfalls:
- Using rng() * i instead of (i + 1), so a card never stays in place.
- Dealing from the start of the array while drawing from the end.
- Sharing one deck array between rounds and mutating it.
Verify:
- [ ] node:test checks the shuffle distribution with a seeded rng.
- [ ] Every rule has a passing and a failing test.
Output: cards.mjs, rules.mjs, ui.js and test/cards.test.mjs.

examples.input: jogo de paciência com embaralhamento justo
examples.output: card ids, Fisher Yates with injected rng, pile model, canPlay reasons, distribution test
